chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Hisham from the one who informed him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A group from those who believed in Musa (peace be upon him) said, 'If we go to the army of Pharaoh and are in it, and gain from his worldly life, then when what we hope for from the victory of Musa (peace be upon him) occurs, we will turn to him.' So they did it. When Musa (peace be upon him) and those with him turned towards the sea, fleeing from Pharaoh, they rode their animals and hastened in their journey to catch up with Musa (peace be upon him) and his army so that they would be with them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent an Angel who struck the faces of their animals and returned them to the army of Pharaoh, so they became among those who drowned with Pharaoh.

And it is reported from Ibn Fazzal from Ali ibn Uqba from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'It is a right upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that you end up with those you lived with in his worldly life.'

key_terms.حَقٌّ عَلَى اللَّهِ: A right upon Allah (a theological concept of divine obligation or fittingness)

ai.seo_question: How did Allah prevent the followers of Musa who joined Pharaoh's army from switching sides at the last moment?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the concept of *al-Tabi'ah* (conformity), where the believers of Musa who sought worldly gain alongside Pharaoh were physically redirected to drown with him, serving as a divine sign of their true spiritual alignment. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) derives the principle that one's eternal fate is determined by the company kept and the context of one's life, a key theme in Shia political theology regarding the legitimacy of ruling authorities and the fate of their followers.
